spec_match.rationale: Opens three real connections (positional string, positional sequence, { protocols } dictionary) against the same-origin /public/echo-socket endpoint and confirms the offer/choice from the server's welcome frame, which is exactly the WebSocketInit contract from whatwg/websockets#76.

interactive.rationale: A real text input drives the offered subprotocol list and Connect populates a five-column results table plus an aria-live detail readout; verified the table filled with server-confirmed rows after clicking Connect.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature-index card promises server-confirmed comparison of both constructor forms and the page delivers precisely that.

edge_cases.rationale: The unsupported-browser branch is first-class: a getter-based support probe drives an honest amber banner, and the dictionary row surfaces the real pre-154 failure rather than a fake success.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5080055102439424 and the WebSocketInit spec PR in see-also.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite probes the exact getter-read contract, both positional forms, the no-subprotocol case, and the duplicate SyntaxError; on Chromium 141 the /conformance/ route ran 5 pass / 1 fail with only the dictionary-read assertion failing, which is the correct pre-154 result.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): clicked Connect, table showed chat / echo / SyntaxError rows confirmed by the server, console had only the page's own logs, no failed same-origin requests (the fonts.googleapis.com cert failure is a sandbox proxy artifact), desktop 1280 and mobile 360 screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads /public/demo-telemetry.js and emits a forms-compared assert with bagOpened/equivalent payload on every run.

design_system.rationale: All colours are CSS variables, page-local button rules set background and color together, controls have 44px min-height, and the page is a live demo rather than a static card.

accessibility.rationale: The input has a real label, the results table has a caption and scoped th cells, the detail readout is an aria-live output, and the support banner is text with aria-hidden icons.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: At 360x740 DPR3 scrollWidth stayed 360 with no clipped controls (screenshot read); the results table wraps via overflow-wrap:anywhere and tap targets are 44px.

openQuestions.title: Correct the fallback copy about what pre-154 browsers do with the dictionary
openQuestions.detail: The detail readout claims a pre-154 browser treats the dictionary 'as a sequence, which stringifies to nothing useful and offers no protocol'. Observed on Chromium 141: the object is coerced to the single subprotocol string '[object Object]', which is invalid, so construction throws SyntaxError before any connection — the table row shows this correctly but the explanatory sentence mispredicts the mechanism (it is not an open-with-no-protocol outcome). One-sentence copy fix in the detail branch for !bagResult.opened.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/add-options-bag-to-websocket-constructor/both-forms/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) per the routine-prompt verification environment. Desktop 1280x2000 and mobile 360x1600 DPR3 screenshots read; Connect exercised via CDP click; server-confirmed rows rendered (chat, echo, SyntaxError for the bag on this pre-154 browser, matching the honest amber support banner); console clean apart from intentional logs; injected 'What this browser supports' panel rendered 5 pass / 1 fail / 6 total, the one fail being the dictionary-read assertion that genuinely needs Chrome 154. The only follow-up is a copy nit in the unsupported-branch explanation.
